caption:
Two days after a midterm election where data centers became a campaign issue, OpenAI made a list of promises to the towns that host them.
It says it will pay for the electricity and grid upgrades its sites use, make a water plan for each location and largely stop using NDAs with public officials.
An ABC News poll found about three quarters of House voters oppose new data centers in their communities.

Would you want an AI data center in your town if it paid its own power bill?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: ABC News, Gizmodo · Photo: abcnews.go.com

site_article.headline: OpenAI pledges to cover data center power costs after midterm backlash
site_article.dek: The company also promised water plans, fewer nondisclosure agreements with officials and local investment, two days after an election in which data centers became a campaign issue.
site_article.summary: On November 5, 2026, OpenAI announced new commitments for communities that host its data centers, including paying for the electricity and energy infrastructure they use. The move followed midterm elections in which candidates opposed to data center growth won key races.
site_article.seo_title: OpenAI pledges to pay data center power costs after midterms
site_article.seo_description: OpenAI says it will pay for its data centers' electricity and grid costs, write local water plans and limit NDAs after a midterm backlash.
site_article.answer_summary: OpenAI said it will pay for the electricity and energy infrastructure used by data centers it owns and operates, create a water plan for each site, largely stop using nondisclosure agreements with public officials and invest in host communities.
site_article.hero_alt: Portrait of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman with a serious expression.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI announced a set of commitments on November 5, 2026 for the communities that host its data centers, two days after midterm elections in which opposition to data center construction featured in several races. According to ABC News and Gizmodo, the company said it will pay for the electricity and energy infrastructure used at its facilities and create a water plan for each location.

ABC News reported that OpenAI will largely end the practice of signing nondisclosure agreements with public officials, with narrow exceptions for security or trade secrets. Gizmodo described the same pledge as a limit on the use of such agreements and said the energy commitment applies to future data centers that OpenAI owns and operates.

The company also said it will form a local compact with the community around each data center to address local concerns and improve transparency, according to ABC News. Gizmodo reported that the commitments are part of what OpenAI calls a National Community Compact and include more openness about construction plans and noise levels.

OpenAI said it will make investments in neighboring communities. ABC News cited examples such as funding free school lunches or improved childcare, while Gizmodo listed childcare, education, healthcare and transportation. ABC News also reported that OpenAI will work with local training providers to help residents get jobs on its data center projects.

Alongside the pledges, OpenAI released a Compute Campus Policy Blueprint, Gizmodo reported. The document calls for rules that would require data center developers to cover electricity costs, be more transparent and work with local communities. In a blog post quoted by ABC News, OpenAI urged federal, state and local policymakers to set clear rules for how the industry builds and said host communities should have a clear say in shaping their futures.

The midterm elections were held on November 3, 2026. Gizmodo reported that Democrats took control of the House and Senate and that local communities across the country passed measures to ban, pause or restrict new data centers.

In Texas, Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa won by 7 percentage points after making opposition to data center construction a central issue, according to ABC News. She supports a moratorium on new construction, stricter water and power rules and an end to tax breaks for data centers. Gizmodo reported that Keisha Lance Bottoms, the incoming governor of Georgia, has also called for pausing data center development.
The ABC News Voter Poll found that about six in 10 House voters nationally said AI is bad for society and that about three quarters opposed new data centers in their own communities.

Gizmodo reported that Chris Lehane, OpenAI's chief global affairs officer, published an essay on November 4 predicting that AI will be the top issue of the 2028 presidential election. OpenAI did not immediately respond to Gizmodo's request for comment.

The pledges address the complaints that have followed large data center projects most closely: higher power bills, water use and deals negotiated out of public view. Most of them are voluntary commitments from a single company, so their effect will depend on how they are written into agreements at each site and whether lawmakers turn the blueprint into binding rules for the whole industry.

Watch whether newly elected officials in Texas, Georgia and other states move ahead with data center pauses or new power and water rules, and whether OpenAI's first local compacts include enforceable terms.
